comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 - that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions - so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists - it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch.
This package is the repo's docs site; it has its own package.json and node_modules, so the repo-root
pinned-versions.json does not cover it and the sweep runs here separately.

@astrojs/starlight.why: Held at the last 0.41.x. Starlight 0.42 deleted `virtual-internal.d.ts` from its package root and ships the `virtual:starlight/*` declarations nowhere else: in 0.42 those modules exist only inside the Vite plugin (`dist/integrations/vite-virtual-modules.js`), and the integration `injectTypes` call covers plugin translations alone. The three component overrides in `src/components/` import five of them - `project-context`, `pagefind-config`, `components/MobileMenuFooter`, `user-config`, `user-images` - so `npm run typecheck` (`astro check`) goes 5x TS2307, plus 2x TS2367 in `scripts/helpers/remark-plugins/custom-admonition-renderer.ts` where the directive node types fall out of scope. All 7 are starlight 0.42: measured green again on 0.41.11 with astro at 7.3.3. The tsconfig `files` entry reaching into `node_modules/@astrojs/starlight/virtual-internal.d.ts` is what breaks, which is the failure AGENTS.md predicted for it - the point of loading starlight's own file was that an upgrade moving it fails the gate rather than going stale in silence. It did. Not fixed here because the remedy is a docs change, not a sweep one: either hand-declare five modules starlight has deliberately made private, or rework the three overrides. 0.41.11 peers `astro ^7.0.2` and `@astrojs/markdown-remark ^7.2.0`, so it holds the rest of this package at their swept versions.
@astrojs/starlight.manualCheck: The check asserts the installed starlight still ships the declaration file the tsconfig `files` entry points at - true on 0.41.x, false from 0.42. It therefore reports the moment the pin is lifted by hand, rather than the moment upstream fixes it. To retry the upgrade: unpin, `npm install`, `npm run typecheck`. Release the pin when starlight ships those declarations again, or once the component overrides no longer import the private virtual modules.

fflate.why: Clears GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98 (fflate unzipSync infinite loop on malformed ZIP64 archives, 0.7.0-0.7.4), fixed in 0.7.5. No direct bump reaches it: satori exact-pins fflate at the vulnerable 0.7.3 and is itself already latest, so nothing the caret sweep floats can move that copy. The forced version is not a hopeful one: this tree already carried 0.7.5 under satori's own @shuding/opentype.js, which declares ^0.7.5, so the override collapses the two copies into one rather than introducing anything. EXACT rather than the caret the repo-root smol-toml override uses, and the difference is deliberate: fflate is 0.x, where a caret pins the minor but ncu rewrites the range anyway, so a caret floor would let the next sweep carry satori from 0.7.x to 0.8.x - a jump ncu itself labels "Major version zero - anything may change" - against a parent that pins one exact patch. An exact pin is invisible to the sweep, which is what this entry is for. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades satori to 0.32.0, and a downgrade is never an acceptable way to clear an advisory.
fflate.manualCheck: The check reads satori's own exact pin, not an installed version, because that pin is what makes the override necessary. When it moves to 0.7.5 or later the override and this entry can both go; if satori moves to a 0.8.x fflate, raise this pin to match rather than dropping it. satori renders the OG images, so `npm run build` is what verifies a change here.

typescript.why: TypeScript 7 (tsgo) does not ship the programmatic compiler API that `astro check` drives: @astrojs/language-server aborts with 'The TypeScript module loaded (found 7.0.2) does not expose the programmatic API that `astro check` relies on'. Same native-API break the repo-root pins against, but reached by a different consumer - docs/ has no ESLint, so typescript-eslint is not the reason here. @astrojs/check peer-requires the range below, so 6.x is the last usable major; the `$typescript` override silences the peer conflict, which is how a sweep reached ^7.0.2 unnoticed (npm install was clean and `npm run build` never invokes `astro check`). Hold until astro supports the native compiler - https://github.com/withastro/roadmap/discussions/1321. The check reads the manifest through fs rather than require(), as the root's does: @astrojs/check has an `exports` map that does not list ./package.json, so require() throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED.
